claim: This type is eight peaking sections parked at fixed centres, one output pan and one level, with a single width byte driving all eight instead of one each. The centres are the named third octaves at 250, 500, 1k, 1.25k, 2k, 3.15k, 4k and 8k: a band raised to the top of its byte and cut to the bottom returns the same centre to within 0.02 octaves, and the eight sit 0.030 octaves under the named series with a scatter of 0.018 -- which is the offset this unit's other equaliser's table was measured to carry, so the two are consistent with one table and this test does not separate that from two readings of one named series. The width byte indexes five entries and four of them are the equaliser's Q byte's entries exactly: 2.583, 1.417, 0.750 and 0.417 octaves between the half-gain points, on a reading whose step is a twelfth. Past the fifth printed step the two types disagree. This one returns the fifth entry and the equaliser returns the first, so what is shared is the table and not the handling of a byte outside it. Each band gain answers over the twenty-five values from 52 to 76 and returns the nearest end for everything outside, and the power-on state is the eight defaults its own page prints, read through a width byte the page prints no default for and which powers up at its third entry.
named: The eight band gains at 40 03 03 through 40 03 0A, the width byte at 40 03 0B and the pan at 40 03 15, on type 01 01.
adds: Three standing claims reach this type for the first time and one of them is cut back. The gain class claim and the width claim did not name 01 01 at all; the pan class claim named it and had never been held against a record on it. What is new beyond that reach is the structure: eight sections at fixed centres is not a shorter equaliser, it is the same sections with the frequency byte removed and replaced by a position in the table, and one width byte serving all eight rather than one per section is the arrangement that makes eight sections cost what four did. The cut is to the width claim, whose rule for a byte past the printed steps holds on the type it was fitted on and not on this one.

document_rows.why: The eleven parameters this type prints and the range against each. Eight of them carry a middle figure, which is where the power-on gains are predicted from; the width byte's range is a list of five with no middle, which is why its own default is measured here rather than read off. Evidence about what a page states and not about the unit.

era_priors.claim: A graphic equaliser of this period shares one width across its sections rather than giving each its own.
era_priors.why: A section's coefficients are recomputed when its width moves. One shared width is one recomputation for eight sections and one byte of state; eight widths are eight of each, which is what makes eight sections cost more than twice what four do.
era_priors.would_be_wrong_if: The page printed a width per band, or the one it prints moved some bands and not others. It prints one, and the one it prints returns the same five entries this unit's parametric equaliser returns from its own per-section width byte -- so the sharing is in how many bytes there are, not in a cheaper filter.

alternatives.reading: The eight centres are the named third octaves themselves, and the 0.030 octaves both this type and the equaliser's table sit under them is carried by the reading rather than by the unit.

separated_by.observable: Where a peaking section of known centre lands when it is rendered and then measured through this stage, on the same band set and the same fit, at each of the eight named third octaves.

predicts.the offset is the reading's: a section rendered at exactly 250 Hz comes back near 241, and the eight rendered centres reproduce the same mean offset of 0.0298 octaves and a scatter near 0.017
predicts.the offset is the unit's: a section rendered at exactly 250 Hz comes back at 250 to within the fit's own spread, so the unit's entries really are below the named series and the two types share a table rather than a name

separated_by.divergence: 0.0298 octaves, which is the mean offset itself: the two readings put a rendered section either side of it.
separated_by.sensitivity_here: The quantity compared is a mean over the eight bands, so what bounds it is the error on that mean and not the spread of one band. The eight offsets scatter by 0.0165 octaves, which is 0.0058 on their mean. Quoted beside it because they answer different questions: how far one band's raised take disagrees with its own cut take runs from 0.0005 to 0.0286 octaves with a median of 0.0027, so a test resting on a single band would have a margin of one and must not be queued. The fitted position is not quantised to the band set, so it is these spreads and not the twelfth-octave step that bound the reading.

run.settings: eight peaking sections rendered one at a time at exactly 250, 500, 1k, 1.25k, 2k, 3.15k, 4k and 8k, at the width this run read the eight through, then measured on the same band set and the same fit the unit's takes were measured on
run.stimulus: the same stimulus, so the comparison carries no correction

alternatives.why_it_matters: Only for what the agreement is evidence of. The eight centres are where they are either way, and so is everything the width byte does.

alternatives.reading: The width byte is not written above its fifth printed step, so what the high settings return is whatever the type was already holding.
alternatives.ruled_out_by: The type powers up with that byte at its third entry, which this run measured rather than assumed -- the takes with nothing written return the third step's profile to a tenth of a decibel across twenty-two bands. A refused write would therefore leave 1.417 octaves between the half-gain points. Bytes five, sixty-four and a hundred and twenty-seven all return 0.417, which is the fifth entry. The write is taken and held at the top of the table.

alternatives.reading: The eighth band is past the end of the table, rather than past what four bits of a frequency byte can reach of it.

separated_by.observable: Where a table entry above 6.3k sits, asked through a byte that indexes the table rather than through a section parked at one of its entries.

predicts.the table ends at the sixteenth entry: nothing indexes an entry above 6166.8, and the eighth band is a section placed outside the table
predicts.the table is longer than four bits reach: an entry near 7900 exists and something indexes it

separated_by.sensitivity_here: Not a question of resolution. The eighth band sits 0.36 octaves above the highest entry the equaliser's byte returns, which is twenty times the scatter of the eight and far outside any reading's own spread. What is missing is a byte to ask with.
separated_by.why_not_separable: No byte in the printed tables indexes a peaking centre above 6.3k. The equaliser's own high corner prints 4k and 8k, but it is a two-state shelf and what it moves is where a slope runs steepest -- 9.5k against 11.3k between its two states, with the profile still rising at the top of the band set in both. That says where a shelf hinges and not where a table entry sits, so it cannot be held against a centre. Until a type is found whose frequency byte reaches past 6.3k, a seventeenth entry and a section outside the table predict the same eight numbers, and this is a margin of one -- the bar this project refuses to queue below.

refuted_by: A band whose raised and cut takes disagree about its centre by more than the spread the other seven show, which would mean the eight are not fixed sections but something whose position moves with its gain. A width setting whose half-gain span differs from the equaliser's at the four entries the band set contains by more than the twelfth of an octave the reading steps in. A gain byte answering outside 52 to 76.
what_it_would_change: Two class claims gain a type and one is cut back. A renderer for this type is eight of the sections the equaliser claim already describes, at seven of the entries the frequency claim already lists and one above them, behind one shared width -- so nothing new has to be modelled for it beyond the fixed positions. And the width claim's rule for a byte past its printed steps becomes a property of the type rather than of the byte, which is the kind of thing a renderer gets wrong silently because no setting a musician uses reaches it.
what_this_does_not_settle: Whether the centres are entries of one shared table or two uses of one named series, which is the standing alternative and costs nothing to settle. What the level byte does, which was not asked. Whether the eight sections are in a chain or summed in parallel: a band profile is magnitude and eight sections at 0 dB are unity either way, which is also why the flat reference this run measured against is the same reference under both. The pan byte's table, which five settings cannot count -- what they say is that its centre sits 2.67 dB under its end, neither the 3.01 of a constant-power pair nor the 6.02 of a crossfade, and that is one figure of a table the pan claim reads nineteen entries in.
what_it_was_predicted_from: The prediction was written before the unit was booked and names what each of the four claims reaching this type would have to return. Two parts of it were wrong and the record of that is worth more than the parts that landed. The width claim's rule for settings past the printed steps was predicted to hold and it does not. And the page's eight printed defaults were predicted to be what the type powers up holding, which they are -- but the prediction could not say what depth they would be read at, because the width byte they are read through is printed as a list with no middle and so has no printed default. That gap was written down before the run and is why the power-on gains were taken again through each of the five widths, which is what put the byte's own default at the third entry.

where_the_eight_sit_hz.why_those_two_lines_are_the_whole_point: They are the same number. A comparison that quotes how much better these eight agree with the equaliser's measured entries than with the named series is quoting a term that sits on both sides of it.

half_gain_span_in_octaves.why_byte_nought_is_not_held_against_the_: The widest entry runs past the ends of the band set, so where its half-gain points fall is set by where the reading stops rather than by the section. The two types differ there by three twelfths and agree exactly at the four entries the band set contains.

the_gain_ladder_on_one_band_db.why_it_is_not_a_decibel_a_step_here: Twelve steps return 11.57 and not 12.00, and four and eight steps return 3.79 and 7.56. A band reading averages over a band, and the peak it is averaging is 0.417 octaves wide against bands a twelfth of an octave apart, so a tall narrow feature is reported shorter than it is. Read at a third of an octave the same takes return 9.7 instead of 11.57, which is the dilution doubling as the band widens. The window and the sticking are read exactly; the step size is not what this reading returns.

what_the_width_byte_powers_up_at.how_it_was_read: The two takes with nothing written to any of the eleven bytes return the profile the third printed step returns, band for band, to a tenth of a decibel over twenty-two bands. The page prints this byte as a list of five figures with no middle, so it names no default for it and the value is measured rather than read off.
